# Torus appendix: a shortest primitive word with linear peak vacancy

Status: AUTHOR_PROVED_UNREVIEWED / RESULT_ONLY_COMPOSE / CONDITIONAL_TYPED_MODEL
Author: Researcher-ID EM-P11-4A56E9; prior contribution identity EM-T6-BFF294
Date: 2026-10-17 UTC
Same SID MCP-387e35a6a7d24e8cb2c44e361b9ce5b9 / RA RA-C193E2AA39B9A6A6DDBB69B3; current36/175.
Author Source: PENDING. Independent review of this new upper bound: PENDING.

## 1. Exact family and the remaining quantitative obligation

Fix an integer m>=3, put n=m^2, and let T=(Z/mZ)^2 with coordinate unit vectors e1,e2. The inventory is exactly I={x_p^a:p in T, a in {0,1,2}}, with 3n distinct members. Its integer encoding may be 1+3(mi+j)+a for p=(i,j), 0<=i,j<m. The only licensed triples are

 A_p={x_p^0,x_(p-e1)^1,x_(p-e2)^2},
 B_p={x_p^0,x_p^1,x_p^2}.                                    (1)

A state is a disjoint matching of these triples. reserve(H) adds one licensed triple if its three members are free, and otherwise leaves the state unchanged. release(x) removes the unique whole present triple containing x, if one exists, and otherwise leaves the state unchanged. There are no extra licensed events, auxiliary members, atomic multi-event swaps or operations outside I.

Each family in (1) separately partitions I, and there is no equality A_p=B_q. A_p meets B_q exactly when p is q, q+e1 or q+e2: the three members of B_q have precisely those A-owners. These facts follow directly from their superscripts and labels.

Vacancy means the number of currently free model members, namely 3n-3|J| for a state J. Start at all A and end at all B. The earlier complete whole proved a lower bound 3 ceil(m/3) on peak vacancy for EVERY legal primitive word, and supplied an upper bound 3m^2. It also proved the minimum command count is 2m^2. This appendix closes the remaining order-of-growth gap in that same exact family:

There is a legal word of exactly 2m^2 commands whose peak vacancy is at most 3(m+1). Therefore the minimum achievable peak p_m satisfies

 3 ceil(m/3) <= p_m <= 3(m+1).                                (2)

Thus p_m=Theta(m), or Theta(sqrt(|I|)), in this square family. No exact value of p_m is asserted. The shortest command count and the new linear upper peak are achieved simultaneously, not by two unrelated words.

## 2. The actual intermediate matchings

For S subset T define

 N(S)=S union(S+e1)union(S+e2),
 J(S)={B_q:q in S} union {A_p:p notin N(S)}.                   (3)

Within each family there is no overlap. The ownership comparison after (1) shows that an A_p in (3) meets none of its selected B_q. Hence J(S) is an actual permitted matching, with

 |J(S)|=|S|+n-|N(S)|,
 vacancy(J(S))=3(|N(S)|-|S|).                                 (4)

In particular J(empty)=all A and J(T)=all B. This construction uses actual members and events, not only an abstract configuration count.

For q notin S let S'=S union {q}. At J(S), the A-events that have to disappear before B_q can be added are exactly the events indexed by

 D=N(S') minus N(S).                                          (5)

Each such A_p is currently present. Release it through the original member x_p^0, once for each p in D, in any fixed order. The release is not an accidental deletion of B_p: p notin N(S) implies p notin S, and its current owner is indeed A_p. Other A-events are disjoint, so preceding releases do not alter that ownership. The already present B-events stay untouched.

After these |D| releases all A-neighbors of B_q have disappeared. Other B-events are disjoint from it, so reserve(B_q) succeeds. The resulting state is exactly J(S'). The argument also covers D empty, when the reserve can occur immediately.

During the releases vacancy only increases, by three per successful release. Just before that reserve it equals

 3(|N(S')|-|S|)
   =3(|N(S')|-|S'|+1).                                       (6)

The reserve then decreases it by three. If no release was needed, (6) is simply the initial vacancy of this transition. This is the actual transient peak calculation; bounding only the post-reserve states would omit a load-bearing intermediate state.

## 3. A finite row order and its complete boundary calculation

Order the points by completing row j=0, then j=1, and so on through j=m-1; in each row use i=0,1,...,m-1. All coordinates in N are still taken modulo m.

Every proper prefix is

 S_(a,b)={all (i,j) with j<a} union {(i,a):0<=i<b},
 0<=a<=m-1, 0<=b<=m-1,                                      (7)

and the final prefix is T. We check |N(S) minus S|<=m at every one of these prefixes, including the initial and wraparound cases.

If a=0,b=0, S is empty. If a=0 and 1<=b<=m-1, the horizontal shift adds just (b,0), while the vertical shift adds the b points (i,1), 0<=i<b. These points lie in different rows and outside S; there are b+1<=m in total.

If 1<=a<=m-2, shifting the last full row upward fills the entire row a. Outside S this contributes the m-b remaining points in row a. Shifting its partial row upward adds the first b points in row a+1. Other shifted full rows are already in S. The only possible new point from horizontally shifting the partial row is (b,a), when b>0; it is already among the m-b remaining row-a points. Thus the two disjoint row contributions give exactly m boundary points. This description also covers b=0, when the first contribution is the entire next row and the second is empty.

If a=m-1, all rows except the last are full. Vertical wraparound from the partial last row lands in the already full row0. The only missing points that N adds are the m-b remaining points in the last row; any horizontal new point is already there. The boundary is therefore m-b<=m.

Finally N(T)=T. Consequently every prefix S in this fixed finite order satisfies

 |N(S)|-|S| <= m.                                             (8)

No disjoint boundaries were added without checking overlap, and no infinite-plane approximation, prime-modulus assumption or unproved expansion result is used.

## 4. Legal shortest word and its transient resource bound

Follow the prefixes in section3. For each newly selected q, perform the actual releases (5), then its successful reserve, as proved in section2. By induction the state after each stage is J(S), so the procedure starts and ends at the specified two full matchings and stays nonoverlapping throughout.

Since S' is again a prefix, (6) and (8) give peak vacancy at most 3(m+1) during every stage; post-reserve vacancy is at most 3m. These statements include every intermediate deletion and both ends of the row sweep. They are an explicit finite legal-word proof, not a reachability computation.

The sets N(S') minus N(S) in the successive stages are pairwise disjoint and their union is N(T) minus N(empty)=T. Thus exactly n old A-events are successfully released, each once. Every q in T is reserved once, so there are exactly n successful reserves and no failed or extra commands: total 2n=2m^2.

For completeness this is a globally shortest word under the literal primitive contract. Every one of the n initial A-events must disappear, and only a release removes one; one release removes at most one. Every one of the n target B-events starts absent and needs its own successful reserve. A primitive cannot do both jobs at once. Hence every word needs at least n releases and n reserves. The constructed word attains this lower bound along with its linear peak bound.

The earlier all-word lower bound, whose actual whole and immutable Source references are supplied below, applies to this same unchanged carrier and includes arbitrary backtracking. Combining it with this explicit new upper proves (2). There is no claim that the row order minimizes the peak constant or that every shortest word has the same resource behavior.
